subject: Transportation Systems
title: Hydrogen-Powered Trains
description: A quick, practical guide to Hydrogen-Powered Trains.

hook.text: Not every rail line has overhead wires. Hydrogen fuel cells could power trains where electrification is too costly.

buildup.text: Germany launched the Coradia iLint in 2022—the world's first hydrogen passenger train in regular service.

discovery.text: The train stores hydrogen on its roof. Fuel cells convert it to electricity. The only emission is water vapor.

twist.text: Hydrogen production itself is energy-intensive. Unless made from renewables, the green benefit shrinks.

climax.text: Battery trains and direct electrification may prove cheaper. Hydrogen's rail future is uncertain.

punchline.text: Hydrogen trains exist. Whether they'll scale is another question.

quiz.question: What does a hydrogen fuel cell train emit?
